0.content: After the Belyi Tsar incited Anastasya and the Third Descender to open a gate to the Abyss, the Heavenly Principles erased Anastasya as punishment. Saarelainen ascended to Celestia and offered his remains to be split into seven pieces to consolidate their system of rule, asking in return that Anastasya be resurrected and that his descendants never be harmed. The Heavenly Principles accepted but required that all of him be forgotten. He bound them with a curse that would take effect only if the promise were broken.

1.comment: Saarelainen: Gnoses and Visions as his remains
1.content: Skirk told Neuvillette in 4.2 that a Gnosis is the "remains of the Third Descender", and Neuvillette told the Traveler. In 7.1 Anastasya says the Gnoses do not originate in Teyvat's system, but from him, and that they amplify their bearers' power.

2.content: In a hidden basement of Zapolyarny Palace there is a seal left by the Third Descender, the last thing he did before he was killed. The Belyi Tsar kept it first and Anastasya after him. Only a Gnosis responds to it; every other attempt to open it has failed. Anastasya thinks the secret inside is vital and may be revealed only when the remains are no longer scattered, which is one of her two reasons for collecting the Gnoses.

3.comment: Saarelainen: Prayer Song XVI of the Hymns of the Far North
3.content: In Nod-Krai the Frostmoon Scions keep a hymn to him as a healer of wounds and sickness. It calls him a cheerful, kind-hearted, noble-born youth who rode a starry steed past Hiisi Island and Pohjola to court the daughter of Pakkaisukko. In this version Pakkaisukko demands that he open the gates of Pohjola, and the Lord of the Seven Calamities carves him into seven pieces. The priestess Ehrnrooth notes that Aila, the first Moonchanter, later simplified the prayer.

4.comment: Saarelainen: Wings of the Silent Moon tale
4.content: A fae folk tale says a snowland king had to cross a realm of pitch-black silence, behind a door deep in the earth, to kill an undying enemy, so a spirit of frost and "a traveler from beyond the palace walls" wove him two wings of ancient moonlight. The wiki connects the pair to Anastasya and Saarelainen. The text itself admits the tale may be a later invention to explain a wind glider.

5.comment: Saarelainen: Stellar Linchpins and his remains (Fontinalia event)
5.content: During the limited-time Sunny Summer Fontinalia event (6.7), Marionette told the Traveler that Fatui research links Stellar Linchpins to the Third Descender: the Heavenly Principles used his remains to make the seven Gnoses to consolidate the Archon system, so Visions, which come from that system, are to some extent related to him; and when a Stellar Linchpin manifests, impurities from his remains are believed to get fixed in place, which would explain the power from beyond Teyvat that Linchpin users often show.
